findings.problem: The candidate tiles that lose (AB 4, CD 6, CE 7) are faded to about 0.4-0.63 opacity and stay on screen for 4-6 s. Their amber-ink text on the pale amber tile then measures about 1.7:1 (darkest text pixel against tile). That breaks the brand rule that text on light uses the -ink shades at 4.5:1: opacity is the only thing lowering it. The weight pills of the dimmed cables in the graph (4 from 7.4 s to 12.4 s, 6 from 9.9 s to 12.4 s) sit at opacity 0.55, about 2.75:1.
findings.fix: Keep every label at opacity 0.8 or more. Show 'not chosen' with the grey tone (c-grey tile: --text-dim text on --panel-2, about 5:1) or let the losing tile fade out completely once the winner is taken. For the graph pills, dim only the cable line and pill face, or hide the pill of a cable that is out of the story, instead of fading the whole pill.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s5@6.5 (abs 46.5 s) and s5@3.2: measured 1.66:1 and 1.99:1 on the AB 4 tile. A scan of effective text opacity every 0.25 s: 'AB 4' local 2.6-6.6 s op 0.13-0.63, 'CD 6' 5.1-9.35 s, 'CE 7' 5.1-11.85 s (op 0.06-0.63 including the fade-in).

findings.problem: Weight pills of the cables that are out of the story are dimmed to opacity 0.4-0.55 (baseO = lerp(1, 0.4, dim)) and stay that way for most of the scene: '6' and '7' from 2.1 s to 13.4 s (about 11 s), '1', '2', '5' for about 4 s at 0.27-0.55. The 28 px digits then read at about 2.0-2.4:1 (down to 1.6:1), below the 3:1 that even large text needs and far below the 4.5:1 the -ink shades are meant to give.
findings.fix: Do not dim the label. Keep pill text at opacity 0.8 or more and make the dimmed state by lightening only the cable line and the pill face and border (grey tone), or hide the pills of cables that are not being discussed (the cut and the swap only need AB, AC, BC, BD, DE).
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s4@3.5 (abs 29.5 s): pill '6' measured 2.43:1 (darkest pixel rgb 166 on white). Opacity scan: '6' and '7' op 0.40-0.55 for 46 samples (local 2.1-13.35 s).

findings.problem: In both panels the weight pills of cables that are not in play sit at opacity 0.4 (about 2.0:1) for most of the 11 s: '4', '6', '7' from 1.6 s to 10.4 s, '1', '2', '3', '5' for 2-5 s each. Digits inside a panel that is meant to be read at a glance are close to unreadable, and they dip to 0.1 opacity on the way.
findings.fix: Same fix as the other scenes: never fade label text below about 0.8. Use grey cables and pills (full-contrast digits) for cables that are not candidates, or hide the pill of any cable that is neither a candidate nor already taken.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s7@5.5 (abs 72.5 s) and s7@8.2: pills '4' and '6' measured 2.39:1. Opacity scan: op 0.10-0.40 for 49-62 samples on '4', '6', '7' (local 1.6-10.35 s).

findings.problem: Once the tree is checked (6.1 s) the three cables that are not in it fade to 0.55 and their weight pills stay at opacity 0.52-0.55 until the end of the scene (about 4 s). The digits 3, 6 and 7 read at 2.6-2.75:1, under the 3:1 large-text floor. Opacity is the only cause (dim = 1 - 0.45 * ramp(t, 6.1, 6.6)).
findings.fix: Keep pill text at full opacity and dim only the cable lines (or fade the pills out together with the cable once the tree is checked). If the cables must stay visible, use the grey tone rather than a global opacity.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s2@8.2 (abs 12.2 s): pills 3, 6, 7 visibly washed out. Opacity scan: op 0.52-0.55 for 16 samples, local 6.6-10.35 s.

findings.problem: From 10.35 s the 'walk' card (and its 151.4) fades to opacity 0.6 and stays there for about 1.5 s until the scene ends. The amber-ink number then reads at about 2.5:1 on its pale card while the new 'never longer' tag is being explained.
findings.fix: Keep the card at full opacity (the number is the thing the next scene compares against), or dim it by changing it to the grey tone.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s9@11.0 (abs 100 s). Opacity scan: '151.4' and 'walk' op 0.6 for 5 samples (local 10.35-11.6 s).

findings.problem: The orange walker token (about 30 px) sits exactly on the town it is visiting and hides that town's letter each time it arrives: A at the start (3.0 s), C at 6.0 s and at every stop of the 12-leg walk. A first-time learner cannot read which town the walker is on without the chip row below.
findings.fix: Offset the token a little above and to the side of the town (or draw it as a small ring round the town) so the letter stays visible.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s9@3.0 (abs 92 s: 'A' covered) and s9@6.0 (abs 95 s: the token overlaps 'C').

findings.problem: The three looping pictograms restart on different periods (4 s, 5 s, 6 s). After they have all been complete once (about 4.5 s) at least one of them is always faded out or reset to bare grey towns, so the last 4 s of the video, and the frame it ends and holds on, show an unfinished recap with an empty icon box. The finished NIC recap (lecture-6) keeps every pictogram complete to the end.
findings.fix: Play each pictogram once and hold its finished state (drop the life() fade-out and the cyc() repeat for the last lap), or stop looping so that all three show their complete drawing from about 4.5 s to the end of the scene.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s11@4.5 (all three complete), then s11@5.5 (row 1 reset), s11@7.4 (row 2 empty), s11@8.3 and s11@8.7 (row 3 reduced to bare towns, row 1 fading). Compare lecture-6 s10@8.7: all rows complete.

findings.problem: (Outside the brand lens but a real misreading.) Each column scales its own bars to its own largest value, so the same quantity is drawn at two very different lengths: Prim for the sparse network (1.0 M) is a 340 px bar, while Prim for the dense network (998 k, almost the same number) is a 66 px bar. A first-time learner reads 'Prim is cheaper on the right' as 'Prim got about five times faster', and the green winner bars (20 k, 998 k) cannot be compared across columns.
findings.fix: Use one scale for both columns (5.0 M = full width, 20 k a minimum sliver), or add a small 'bars scaled per network' note. With one shared scale the left column is still clear because the 20 k sliver against 1.0 M is the point.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s8@8.2 (abs 86.2 s): left 1.0 M bar spans x 85-424, right 998 k bar x 553-619, right 5.0 M bar x 553-891.

findings.problem: After the swap the cost counter counts down 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 in the solid green 'kept' tone over 0.6 s. While every cable is already green (the 11-cost tree) it shows 12, which is the number of the dearer tree T, so for a moment the green tree is labelled with the wrong cost.
findings.fix: Switch directly from 15 (red) to 11 (green) with a pop, or run the count-down while the box is still red and turn it green only when it lands on 11.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s4@10.5 (abs 36.5 s): green 'tree cost 12' above the green AC BC BD DE tree.

findings.problem: Several items break the 'everything inside the stage with at least 12 px margin' rule (stage is x 72-1008, y 262-902): scene 3 labels '5 towns', '8 towns', '20 towns' start at x = 72 and 'every pair of towns linked' ends at y = 898 (4 px from the bottom); scene 8 tags 'Road map: few cables' and 'Every pair linked' start at y = 262 (0 px from the top) and the 'same tree either way' pill ends at y = 899 with its lip; scene 6 sorted-list tiles start at y = 268 and scene 7 panels at y = 270; scene 7 'total = total' cards and the scene 10 number-line value tags end at y = 896 including the 6 px lip (6 px margin); scene 5 'start' and 'ignored' tags sit at x = 74-78.
findings.fix: Shift those groups 8-14 px inward (for example drop the tag row in scene 8 and the tile row in scene 6 by 12 px, move the scene 3 labels to x = 84, lift the scene 7 totals and the scene 10 line up by 10 px).
findings.evidence: DOM bounding boxes sampled every 0.3 s over the whole video. Stills: s8@2.8 (tags touch the stage top), s3@10.8, s7@10.8, s10@9.8.

findings.problem: Colour roles overload in places, although the storyboard sanctions it: purple means the cut in scenes 4, 7 and 11 but the best possible tour in scene 10 (where the same scene also draws a red cut), and orange means 'candidates under test' in scenes 4-7 but the doubled walk in scenes 9-10. A learner who has just learned 'purple = the cut' meets a purple dashed tour.
findings.fix: If the storyboard can change, give the best-tour benchmark a neutral dashed grey outline with a purple 'best' label, or keep it purple and say so in the tag ('best tour'). Otherwise accept as is: the tags in scene 10 already name each colour.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-4 s10@2.5 (purple dashed tour) against s4@3.5 (purple cut) and s9@6.0 (orange walk) against s5@9.8 (orange candidates).

findings.problem: Determinism check. update(t) is pure by source (grep for Math.random, Date, setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame, transition, animation, performance finds nothing in videos/a4 or videos/l5/common.js; the only randomness is the seeded mulberry32 helper). Seeking the same absolute times in three different orders gave identical DOM style values for every visible element (no opacity, visibility, left, top, width, colour or transform difference over 343 times; only hidden elements keep stale attributes). Screenshots in the same order are byte-identical (fwd vs fwd again: 0 differing pixels), but forward vs reverse order differs in 18 of 32 sampled frames: 2-8 pixels by at most 4 levels in most, up to 671 pixels by up to 57 levels in 3 frames (the scale-popping W and 75.7 tags in scene 10, local 3.9 s, and a few edge pixels of town A in scene 5, local 2.0 and 9.4 s). The cause is Chromium re-rasterising scaled layers depending on frame history, not scene state.
findings.fix: No scene change needed. Keep tools/render-video.js rendering each worker's frames in increasing time order. If a shimmer is ever seen on popping tags in the mp4, render with a single worker or pin raster scale with will-change: transform on the tags.
findings.evidence: md5 and pixel comparison of 32 times (1.3 s to 116 s, step 3.7 s) in forward, reverse and shuffled order; DOM style comparison at 343 times; cause shown by cropping s10 at abs 104.9 s in both orders.
